flashcards.front: What is the mechanism through which TSST causes Toxic shock syndrome?
flashcards.back: TSST is a superantigenic exotoxin, it binds to and activates T cells with no specificity to an antigen. This causes all activated T cells to secrete large amounts of interleukins resulting in a cytokine storm and shock

flashcards.front: Explain the development of antibiotic resistant S.aureus.
flashcards.back:
Firstly, it developed a resistance to penicillin by acquiring a plasmid that codes for the production of B-lactamase, this was overcome by introducing B-lactamase resistant penicillin like nafcillin and methicillin.
Secondly, some strains acquired resistance to these drugs (MRSA and VRSA) by changing a sequence of genes on a region of their chromosome (SCCmec) to give rise to 2 genes (mecA and mec C) that produce a low affinity penicillin binding protein (PBP2a), this was overcome by introducing vancomycin. 
Lastly, these strains also acquired resistance to vancomycin through the van gene acquired from enterococci by plasmids 
They are now treated by other classes of antibiotics like tetracyclines, erythromycin, aminoglycosides
